iupac.title: Murray et al. (2013). Definitions of terms relating to mass spectrometry (IUPAC Recommendations 2013). Pure and Applied Chemistry 85, 1515–1609.
iupac.note: Terminology and definitions; DOI metadata verified via the authors' university repository.

nist.title: NIST Standard Reference Database 1A: Mass Spectral Libraries.
nist.note: Official overview of EI and tandem mass-spectral reference collections.

isotopes.title: NIST. Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions with Relative Atomic Masses.
isotopes.note: Isotope masses and representative compositions; sample abundances can vary.

esi.title: Fenn et al. (1989). Electrospray ionization for mass spectrometry of large biomolecules. Science 246, 64–71.
esi.note: Primary study of electrospray for large biomolecules. DOI: 10.1126/science.2675315.

orbitrap.title: Makarov (2000). Electrostatic axially harmonic orbital trapping: a high-performance technique of mass analysis. Analytical Chemistry 72, 1156–1162.
orbitrap.note: Primary description of the Orbitrap principle. DOI: 10.1021/ac991131p.

etd.title: Syka et al. (2004). Peptide and protein sequence analysis by electron transfer dissociation mass spectrometry. PNAS 101, 9528–9533.
etd.note: Primary study of electron-transfer dissociation of peptide cations.

dia.title: Gillet et al. (2012). Targeted data extraction of the MS/MS spectra generated by data-independent acquisition: a new concept for consistent and accurate proteome analysis. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 11, O111.016717.
dia.note: Primary study underlying SWATH-style DIA extraction. DOI: 10.1074/mcp.O111.016717.

mzml.title: HUPO Proteomics Standards Initiative. mzML specification and documentation.
mzml.note: Authoritative format specification and controlled-vocabulary resources.

pwiz.title: Kessner et al. (2008). ProteoWizard: open source software for rapid proteomics tools development. Bioinformatics 24, 2534–2536.

fdr.title: Elias & Gygi (2007). Target-decoy search strategy for increased confidence in large-scale protein identifications by mass spectrometry. Nature Methods 4, 207–214.
fdr.note: Primary methodological discussion of target–decoy error estimation. DOI: 10.1038/nmeth1019.

codata.title: NIST. CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: proton mass in u and electron mass in u.
codata.note: Official constants table. Examples round the proton mass to 1.007276467 Da; u and Da name the same mass unit.

carbon.title: NIST. Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions for Carbon.
carbon.note: Representative carbon-13 fraction 0.0107 and carbon-13 mass 13.00335483507 Da. Teaching models hold these inputs fixed; natural sample compositions vary.

measurement.title: Waters. The Mass Spectrometry Primer: Mass Accuracy & Resolution.
measurement.note: Official manufacturer explanation of calibration, interference, and measurement conditions. Used for principles, not current product performance claims.

esi-mechanisms.title: Konermann, Ahadi, Rodriguez & Vahidi (2013). Unraveling the mechanism of electrospray ionization. Analytical Chemistry 85, 2–9.
esi-mechanisms.note: Mechanistic review of ion evaporation, charged residue, and chain ejection; models apply to different analyte and experimental regimes. Metadata and abstract verified through PubMed PMID 23134552.

protein-esi.title: Konermann, Metwally, Duez & Peters (2019). Charging and supercharging of proteins for mass spectrometry: recent insights into the mechanisms of electrospray ionization. Analyst 144, 6157–6171.
protein-esi.note: Review connecting native-like and denaturing protein experiments to different charging mechanisms and documenting condition dependence. Metadata and abstract verified through PubMed PMID 31560020.

maldi-mechanisms.title: Knochenmuss (2006). Ion formation mechanisms in UV-MALDI. Analyst 131, 966–986.
maldi-mechanisms.note: Critical review distinguishing primary ion generation from subsequent plume reactions and discussing competing mechanistic descriptions. Publisher metadata and abstract, and indexed author-manuscript passages, checked.

maldi-peptides.title: Sandoval (2014). Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Time-of-Flight Mass Analysis of Peptides. Current Protocols in Protein Science 77, 16.2.1–16.2.11.
maldi-peptides.note: Peptide-analysis protocol supporting the qualified expectation of predominantly singly protonated MALDI peptide ions. Does not justify a universal charge-state or salt-tolerance claim. Metadata and abstract verified through PubMed PMID 25081740.

maldi-multicharge.title: Trimpin, Inutan, Herath & McEwen (2010). Laserspray ionization, a new atmospheric pressure MALDI method for producing highly charged gas-phase ions of peptides and proteins directly from solid solutions. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 9, 362–367.
maldi-multicharge.note: Primary experimental counterexample to the claim that all matrix-assisted laser methods produce only singly charged ions. This specialized atmospheric-pressure method is not presented as conventional vacuum MALDI. Metadata and abstract verified through PubMed PMID 19955086.

esi-suppression.title: King, Bonfiglio, Fernandez-Metzler, Miller-Stein & Olah (2000). Mechanistic investigation of ionization suppression in electrospray ionization. Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry 11, 942–950.
esi-suppression.note: Primary experiments on biological extracts support a role for nonvolatile solutes and changed droplet properties in ESI suppression. The article does not generalize this into the only suppression mechanism. Publisher metadata and abstract verified.

maldi-dynamics.title: Knochenmuss (2016). The Coupled Chemical and Physical Dynamics Model of MALDI. Annual Review of Analytical Chemistry 9, 365–385.
maldi-dynamics.note: Mechanistic review covering positive and negative ionization, charge-transfer reactions, suppression, and experimental-condition dependence. Its named model is not treated as the sole universally established mechanism. Publisher abstract and metadata verified.

maldi-adducts.title: Leite, Hajivandi, Diller & Pope (2004). Removal of sodium and potassium adducts using a matrix additive during matrix-associated laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometric analysis of peptides. Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry 18, 2953–2959.
maldi-adducts.note: Primary peptide experiments document alkali-metal adduct patterns and matrix-cluster interference; used to qualify salt-tolerance claims. Metadata and abstract verified through PubMed PMID 15536629.

charge-number.title: IUPAC (1994). Quantities and units for electrophoresis in the clinical laboratory. Pure and Applied Chemistry 66, 891–896.
charge-number.note: Page 893 defines an ion's signed charge number as electric charge divided by the elementary charge; positive for cations, negative for anions.

adduct-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Adduct ion, entry A00139.
adduct-definition.note: Atom retention and association in the definition of an adduct ion; read alongside the revised 2013 mass-spectrometry recommendations.

sodium.title: NIST. Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions for Sodium.
sodium.note: Neutral sodium-23 relative atomic mass 22.9897692820; the example subtracts one electron mass to approximate sodium-cation mass.

isotopologue-definition.title: IUPAC (1994). Glossary of terms used in physical organic chemistry: isotopologue and isotopomer.
isotopologue-definition.note: Definitions distinguish isotope composition from isotope positions. The linked IUPAC glossary provides both entries.

monoisotopic-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Monoisotopic mass, entry 12495.
monoisotopic-definition.note: Defines the isotope choice as the most abundant isotope of each element; derived from IUPAC Recommendations 2013.

exact-mass-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Exact mass, entry 12407.
exact-mass-definition.note: A calculated mass for a specified isotope composition; not synonymous with experimentally measured accurate mass.

hydrogen.title: NIST. Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions for Hydrogen.
hydrogen.note: Neutral hydrogen-1 relative atomic mass 1.00782503223, used in the water example.

oxygen.title: NIST. Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions for Oxygen.
oxygen.note: Oxygen-16 and oxygen-18 relative atomic masses 15.99491461957 and 17.99915961286, with representative isotope compositions.

average-mass-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Average mass, entry 12341.
average-mass-definition.note: Mass weighted by isotopic composition; distinct from monoisotopic mass.

vim-accuracy.title: JCGM. International Vocabulary of Metrology, VIM3, entry 2.13: measurement accuracy.
vim-accuracy.note: Accuracy is a qualitative concept and is distinguished from precision; the entry includes informative annotations.

vim-error.title: JCGM. International Vocabulary of Metrology, VIM3, entry 2.16: measurement error.
vim-error.note: Defines error as measured value minus reference value; basis of the explicitly signed example.

mass-accuracy-usage.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Mass accuracy, entry 09406.
mass-accuracy-usage.note: Surface-analysis terminology from IUPAC Recommendations 2020 uses measured mass minus reference mass; included to make differing conventions explicit.

vim-precision.title: JCGM. International Vocabulary of Metrology, VIM3, entry 2.15: measurement precision.
vim-precision.note: Agreement among replicate measurements under specified conditions; not a synonym for accuracy.

accurate-mass-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Accurate mass, entry 12326.
accurate-mass-definition.note: Experimentally determined ion mass of known charge; distinguishes measured accurate mass from calculated exact mass.

resolution-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Resolution in mass spectroscopy, entry R05318 (archived edition).
resolution-definition.note: Documents FWHM and 10% valley conventions. Historical terminology is read alongside the IUPAC Recommendations 2013 discussion, rather than treated as a universal naming rule.

quadrupole-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer, entry 12602.
quadrupole-definition.note: Definition from IUPAC Recommendations 2013, p. 1597. Supports the four-rod RF/DC stability-filter principle; no product performance claims.

quadrupole-scanning.title: Shimadzu. Introduction to mass analyzers: Quadrupole MS.
quadrupole-scanning.note: Official explanation of scanning RF/DC amplitudes and selected-ion monitoring. Used only for the quadrupole scanning mechanism, without generalizing the page's product comparisons or specifications.

rf-only-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. RF-only quadrupole, entry 12560.
rf-only-definition.note: Definition from IUPAC Recommendations 2013, p. 1587. Supports distinguishing a broad-transmission ion guide with a low-m/z cutoff from an RF/DC mass filter.

tof-principles.title: JEOL USA. Mass Spectrometry Basics: Time-of-flight and Reflectron.
tof-principles.note: Official explanation of time-based mass analysis and energy-spread compensation by a reflectron. Used for mechanisms only; comparative rankings and general performance specifications are excluded.

linear-ion-trap.title: Schwartz, Senko & Syka (2002). A two-dimensional quadrupole ion trap mass spectrometer. Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry 13, 659–669.
linear-ion-trap.note: Primary demonstration of mass-selective ejection, resonance excitation, isolation, and MSn in a linear quadrupole ion trap. DOI: 10.1016/S1044-0305(02)00384-7. Results from that instrument are not universal family specifications.

space-charge-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Space charge effect, entry 12577.
space-charge-definition.note: Definition from IUPAC Recommendations 2013, p. 1591. Mutual repulsion can perturb ion trajectories, particularly when many ions are confined to a small volume.

orbitrap-detection.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific. Orbitrap Excedion Series Operating Manual: Measuring principle.
orbitrap-detection.note: Official documentation of axial oscillations, split-electrode image-current detection, and Fourier transformation. Used only for the measurement principle, not model-specific specifications.

fticr-origin.title: Comisarow & Marshall (1974). Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance spectroscopy. Chemical Physics Letters 25, 282–283.
fticr-origin.note: Primary demonstration of pulsed excitation, time-domain detection, and Fourier transformation. Publisher abstract and metadata verified; historical performance numbers are not used as modern specifications.

fticr-frequency.title: Nagornov, Kozhinov & Tsybin (2017). Fourier Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance Mass Spectrometry at the Cyclotron Frequency. Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry 28, 768–780.
fticr-frequency.note: Primary study distinguishing the unperturbed cyclotron frequency from the reduced cyclotron frequency normally measured in a trapped-ion experiment. DOI: 10.1007/s13361-017-1598-y. Supports the boundary on the introductory ideal equation.

ftms-processing.title: Michalski et al. (2012). Ultra High Resolution Linear Ion Trap Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer (Orbitrap Elite) Facilitates Top Down LC MS/MS and Versatile Peptide Fragmentation Modes. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 11, O111.013698.
ftms-processing.note: Primary instrument study showing that field geometry and phase-aware Fourier processing influence resolving power at a given transient duration and that parallel acquisition affects cycle time. DOI: 10.1074/mcp.O111.013698. Used for those dependencies, not product comparisons.

analyzer-overview.title: Scripps Research. Basics of Mass Spectrometry: Mass Analyzers.
analyzer-overview.note: Institutional tutorial supporting the mass analyzer's role in measuring gas-phase ions by m/z and distinguishing ionization, analysis, and detection. Used for stable principles, not dated rankings or specifications.

hcd-primary.title: McAlister et al. (2011). Higher-energy collision-activated dissociation without a dedicated collision cell. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 10, O111.009456.
hcd-primary.note: Primary instrument study; the accessible abstract distinguishes beam-type HCD from resonant-excitation collisional activation. DOI: 10.1074/mcp.O111.009456. Used for method classification, not a universal performance ranking.

ecd-primary.title: Zubarev, Kelleher & McLafferty (1998). Electron Capture Dissociation of Multiply Charged Protein Cations. A Nonergodic Process. Journal of the American Chemical Society 120, 3265–3266.
ecd-primary.note: Primary ECD demonstration, including electron capture, charge reduction, backbone products, and intact charge-reduced ions. The mechanistic interpretation in the title is not presented as universally settled.

etd-supplemental.title: Swaney et al. (2007). Supplemental activation method for high-efficiency electron-transfer dissociation of doubly protonated peptide precursors. Analytical Chemistry 79, 477–485.
etd-supplemental.note: Primary study of charge-reduced products and supplemental activation of doubly protonated peptides. DOI: 10.1021/ac061457f. Supports qualified ETD charge-state scope rather than an absolute exclusion of 2+ precursors.

peptide-nomenclature.title: Chu et al. (2015). Proposed nomenclature for peptide ion fragmentation. International Journal of Mass Spectrometry 390, 24–27.
peptide-nomenclature.note: Primary nomenclature proposal discussing conventional terminal-series labels and the need to specify charge, radicals, and hydrogen changes. The Guide uses familiar lower-case peptide labels with explicit charge/radical clarification; it does not declare the proposed system a universal standard.

neutral-loss-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Neutral loss, entry 12505.
neutral-loss-definition.note: Definition from IUPAC Recommendations 2013, p. 1571. Supports distinguishing the uncharged species lost from the charged residual product.

nitrogen.title: NIST. Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions for Nitrogen.
nitrogen.note: Nitrogen-14 relative atomic mass 14.00307400443, used with carbon-12, hydrogen-1, and oxygen-16 in the constructed alanine-residue calculation.

coisolation-primary.title: Yu, Deng & Nesvizhskii (2025). MSFragger-DDA+ enhances peptide identification sensitivity with full isolation window search. Nature Communications 16, 3329.
coisolation-primary.note: Primary study of cofragmented peptides in DDA spectra, including narrow-window data. DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-58728-z. Used to establish mixed-spectrum risk, without transferring prevalence or performance figures to other experiments.

ms-order.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific. Orbitrap Tribrid Series Getting Started Guide: Glossary, scan power.
ms-order.note: Official glossary, printed p. 145. Supports the common instrument convention MS1, MS2, MS3 as successive stages of mass analysis. Used for notation only; the exponent is not an acquisition-cycle number. Official indexed glossary text verified; direct PDF retrieval failed in this pass.

dda-selection.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific. Orbitrap Tribrid Apex Small Molecule Method Editor Help: Data-dependent properties pane.
dda-selection.note: Official explanation of Top N as an upper number of dependent scans and cycle-time-limited acquisition as a different scheduling mode. No default settings or product-performance claims are transferred.

dynamic-exclusion.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific. Orbitrap Ascend Method Editor Help: Dynamic Exclusion filter.
dynamic-exclusion.note: Official documentation of repeat count, exclusion duration, and mass matching. Used to explain temporary precursor-selection exclusion, not to recommend universal parameters.

isolation-window.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific. Orbitrap Exploris 120 Software Manual: Data-Dependent MS2 Properties pane.
isolation-window.note: Official explanation of isolation full width and offset, sensitivity/interference tradeoffs, and the distinction between maximum injection time and actual accumulation. Numeric teaching windows are independently constructed.

srm-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Selected reaction monitoring, entry 12568.
srm-definition.note: Definition from IUPAC Recommendations 2013, p. 1589; includes the relationship to multiple reaction monitoring. Official indexed definition verified; direct page retrieval was unavailable during this research pass.

prm-primary.title: Peterson et al. (2012). Parallel reaction monitoring for high resolution and high mass accuracy quantitative, targeted proteomics. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 11, 1475–1488.
prm-primary.note: Primary PRM study, DOI: 10.1074/mcp.O112.020131. Supports recording a product spectrum for a selected precursor and extracting product signals afterward. Official PubMed metadata and indexed PMC text verified; study-specific comparisons are not universal rankings.

targeted-scheduling.title: AB SCIEX (2012). Scheduled MRM Algorithm Tutorial, Analyst 1.6.1 Software.
targeted-scheduling.note: Official tutorial, especially printed pp. 3–7, explains retention-time scheduling and the need to cover both the peak and retention-time variation. No source screenshot, recommended starting setting, or vendor throughput claim is reproduced.

targeted-timing.title: SCIEX. How to choose the appropriate dwell time/cycle time in an MRM and sMRM method to get enough points per chromatographic peak.
targeted-timing.note: Official timing equations for dwell, pause, active transitions, and cycle time. Used for the simplified serial model; platform-specific defaults and universal sampling thresholds are excluded.

extracted-ion-profile.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Extracted ion profile, entry 12410.
extracted-ion-profile.note: Definition from IUPAC Recommendations 2013, p. 1542. Explicitly includes extracted ion chromatograms among time-dependent selected-m/z traces. Official indexed definition verified; direct page retrieval returned 403.

xic-traces.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific. Compound Discoverer 3.4 User Guide: Chromatograms view traces.
xic-traces.note: Official explanation of total-ion, base-peak, and extracted-ion chromatograms. Supports the distinction between a spectrum and a selected-m/z trace; no software workflow is prescribed.

xic-settings.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific. Compound Discoverer 3.4 User Guide: Create Mass Trace node.
xic-settings.note: Official definitions of MS-order/polarity filters and ppm extraction bounds. Supports the constructed centroid-summation example; the example is not experimental data or a recommended tolerance.

psi-ms-representation.title: HUPO-PSI. PSI-MS controlled vocabulary: peak picking, centroid spectrum, and profile spectrum.
psi-ms-representation.note: Official controlled vocabulary, inspected data version 4.2.2 (2026-09-18). Entries MS:1000035, MS:1000127, and MS:1000128 support representation boundaries; no universal centroid-intensity algorithm is inferred.

msconvert-filters.title: ProteoWizard. msconvert technical documentation: peakPicking filter.
msconvert-filters.note: Official software documentation. Supports algorithm and MS-level selection and recording processing choices. Indexed filter text was verified; direct page extraction returned minimal content. No version-dependent command recipe or defaults are prescribed.

feature-finding.title: OpenMS. FeatureFinderMetabo documentation.
feature-finding.note: Official developer documentation of assembling compatible mass traces into metabolite features and separating elution profiles. Used as an implementation example, not a universal definition or parameter prescription. Documentation inspected 2026-10-06.

msi-chemical-analysis.title: Sumner et al. (2007). Proposed minimum reporting standards for chemical analysis. Metabolomics 3, 211–221.
msi-chemical-analysis.note: MSI Chemical Analysis Working Group reporting recommendations. Supports evidence-specific identification of previously characterized metabolites and calibration/validation reporting. Publisher metadata/abstract, indexed PMC text, and an institutional author manuscript (Fiehn Lab, UC Davis), p. 12, were checked. The institutional manuscript is not the final typeset version. Historical numerical validation thresholds are not adopted.

fdr-original.title: Benjamini & Hochberg (1995). Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B 57, 289–300.
fdr-original.note: Original definition of FDR as the expectation of the false-discovery proportion, with zero when there are no discoveries. Publisher metadata and abstract verified. The Guide illustrates the definition without prescribing the BH procedure or assuming arbitrary dependence is allowed.

normalization-comparison.title: Kauko et al. (2015). Label-free quantitative phosphoproteomics with novel pairwise abundance normalization reveals synergistic RAS and CIP2A signaling. Scientific Reports 5, 13099.
normalization-comparison.note: Original phosphoproteomics experiment. DOI: 10.1038/srep13099. Full publisher text supports the risk of centering when genuine global directional changes violate stability assumptions. Its pairwise method and biological conclusions are not generalized to all data.

missingness-benchmark.title: Harris, Fondrie, Oh & Noble (2023). Evaluating Proteomics Imputation Methods with Improved Criteria. Journal of Proteome Research 22, 3427–3438.
missingness-benchmark.note: Original benchmark across proteomics workflows. Supports experiment- and task-dependent imputation performance and the need for an unimputed comparator. Metadata/abstract and indexed primary PMC text (PMC10949645) verified; direct PMC access encountered a bot check. No method is recommended universally.

mqacc-reporting.title: Kirwan et al. (2022). Quality assurance and quality control reporting in untargeted metabolic phenotyping: mQACC recommendations for analytical quality management. Metabolomics 18, 70.
mqacc-reporting.note: Consortium reporting recommendations, not binding regulation. Full publisher text supports distinguishing blanks, pooled/reference QC, suitability tests, placement, acceptance criteria, and drift assessment in untargeted metabolomics.

analysis-reporting.title: Goodacre et al. (2007). Proposed minimum reporting standards for data analysis in metabolomics. Metabolomics 3, 231–241.
analysis-reporting.note: MSI reporting recommendations. Publisher text supports recording design, acquisition scheduling, preprocessing, algorithms, validation splits, and blind testing. The batch-confounding example and modern audit checklist are explicitly pedagogical reasoning built on those principles.

mztab-m.title: HUPO-PSI and MSI. mzTab-M 2.0 metabolomics results specification.
mztab-m.note: Official released format specification. Sections 5.2 and 5.4 distinguish samples/assays/runs and missing-data encoding; sections 6.3–6.5 distinguish molecule summaries, features, and identification evidence. A format declaration does not verify biological independence or determine the missing-data mechanism.

base-peak-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Base peak in mass spectrometry, entry B00608.
base-peak-definition.note: Current Gold Book entry retaining the 1991 recommendation: the greatest-intensity peak in a mass spectrum. Official indexed definition verified; direct retrieval returned 403. Does not assign molecular identity.

relative-intensity-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Intensity (relative to base peak) in mass spectrometry, entry I03073.
relative-intensity-definition.note: Defines the intensity ratio to the strongest resolved peak, conventionally scaled to base peak = 100. Also verified against IUPAC Recommendations 2013, entry 220. Official indexed text verified; direct retrieval returned 403.

retention-time-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Total retention time in column chromatography, entry 10039.
retention-time-definition.note: Definition from Terminology of separation methods (IUPAC Recommendations 2017): injection to the relevant peak maximum; includes hold-up time. Official indexed definition verified; direct retrieval returned 403. The short Guide orientation uses this conventional total-retention-time meaning.

sep-sample-handbook.title: Agilent Technologies. Sample Preparation Fundamentals for Chromatography. Publication 5991-3326EN.
sep-sample-handbook.note: Official manufacturer handbook, cover and full text checked. Used for categories of preparation and general LLE/SPE principles, especially chapters 2, 7 and 10. No product ranking, universal assay requirement, or detailed hazardous procedure is adopted.

sep-ppt-study.title: Waters (2020). Simple Approach for the Removal of Phospholipids in Small Molecule Quantitative Bioanalysis Using Ostro Sample Preparation Plates.
sep-ppt-study.note: Official application note, full text checked. Used narrowly for the fact that protein precipitation can leave soluble matrix constituents, including lipids. Product superiority claims, assay performance, and experimental recipes are not generalized or reproduced.

sep-recovery-matrix.title: Waters (2018). Bioanalytical Sample Preparation and Method Development for Therapeutic and Endogenous Peptides. Reference card 720006298.
sep-recovery-matrix.note: Official technical reference, full PDF checked. PDF pages 10–12 distinguish pre-extraction, post-extraction and neat comparisons and define recovery and matrix factor; page 2 discusses surface binding. Used for conceptual comparisons only, not peptide-specific preparation recipes or blanket container recommendations. A/B/C numbers in the wiki are original constructed examples.

sep-m10.title: FDA / ICH (2022). M10 Bioanalytical Method Validation and Study Sample Analysis. Final guidance.
sep-m10.note: Official final FDA PDF, November 2022, checked. Sections 3.2.6, 3.2.8 and 7.3 support carryover assessment context, stability evaluation and recovery consistency. Scope is bioanalytical assays supporting drug-development submissions. No universal acceptance limits for unrelated MS applications are claimed.

sep-matrix-assessment.title: Matuszewski, B. K., Constanzer, M. L. & Chavez-Eng, C. M. (2003). Strategies for the assessment of matrix effect in quantitative bioanalytical methods based on HPLC-MS/MS. Analytical Chemistry 75(13), 3019–3030.
sep-matrix-assessment.note: Primary study. Author, title, volume, pages, DOI and abstract verified through PubMed PMID 12964746 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12964746/); ACS full-text retrieval was unavailable. Abstract supports distinguishing matrix effect and true recovery; exact teaching-ratio definitions are independently verified in the official Waters technical reference. No claim of full-paper inspection.

sep-retention-factor.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Retention factor in column chromatography, entry R05359.
sep-retention-factor.note: Official indexed definition and legacy official page checked. Adjusted retention time divided by hold-up time. Direct current-page retrieval returned 403; official search-index text supplied the definition. The Guide explicitly bounds its numerical example to an appropriate isocratic model.

sep-separation-modes.title: Waters. Liquid Chromatography Separation Modes.
sep-separation-modes.note: Official manufacturer overview checked. Used for qualitative reversed-phase and HILIC mode distinctions and typical gradient directions. Product lists, popularity claims and numerical solvent recipes are excluded; no universal elution-order claim is made.

sep-lc-handbook.title: Agilent Technologies. The LC Handbook: Guide to LC Columns and Method Development.
sep-lc-handbook.note: Official handbook, full PDF checked. Relevant sections cover dwell volume and method transfer, sample injection/extra-column broadening, and LC-MS-compatible mobile phases. Dwell delay is volume divided by flow; a contradictory glossary typo is not adopted. Constructed examples do not reproduce vendor application data or universal operating limits.

sep-peak-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Peak in chromatography, entry P04451.
sep-peak-definition.note: Official indexed PDF and legacy official HTML definition checked. Includes unresolved peaks containing multiple components. Direct current-page retrieval returned 403. Used for the elution-time peak concept, not chemical identification or quantification.

sep-peak-area.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Peak area in chromatography, entry P04453.
sep-peak-area.note: Official indexed PDF definition checked: area enclosed by peak and baseline. Constructed triangle calculations are original teaching examples, not empirical peak models or prescribed integration methods.

sep-epa-blanks.title: US EPA (2018). SW-846, Chapter Three: Inorganic Analytes, Revision 6, Update VI.
sep-epa-blanks.note: Official PDF, title/date and section 3.1 definition of method blank checked. Used only for the methodological purpose of testing preparation/equipment/reagent contamination. Inorganic-specific procedures, sampling requirements and acceptance limits are not transferred to LC-MS.

sep-carryover.title: Waters. Alliance iS System support: Carryover, topic LCI-USG-0023.
sep-carryover.note: Official support page checked. Supports residual previously injected material and sequence-dependent carryover. Instrument-specific carryover specification, wash recipes and timing settings are excluded.

sep-carryover-diagnostics.title: Waters. What are some tips for troubleshooting carryover or ghost peaks on my LC column? WKB246120.
sep-carryover-diagnostics.note: Official support article checked. Used narrowly for controlled gradient/injection-volume/vial comparisons and multiple possible sources. The Guide does not reproduce the operational procedure or present a diagnostic pattern as unique proof.

quant-vim-calibration.title: JCGM. International Vocabulary of Metrology, VIM3, entry 2.39: calibration.
quant-vim-calibration.note: Official definition distinguishes establishing and using a measurement relationship from instrument adjustment. Concentration-calibration examples are independently constructed.

quant-vim-curve.title: JCGM. International Vocabulary of Metrology, VIM3, entry 4.31: calibration curve.
quant-vim-curve.note: Official definition and note: a curve relates indication and measured quantity value but does not itself supply measurement uncertainty.

quant-ich-m10.title: ICH (2022). M10: Bioanalytical Method Validation and Study Sample Analysis. Final version adopted 24 May 2022.
quant-ich-m10.note: Official final guideline, sections 1.3, 3.1, 3.2.4–3.2.7. Supports internal-standard suitability, calibration-model reporting, independent QC preparation, and validated dilution. Its regulated drug-bioanalysis scope is stated; numerical regulatory acceptance thresholds are not generalized to exploratory omics. ICH copyright acknowledged; explanations are original and are not ICH-endorsed translations.

quant-nist-residuals.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 4.4.4: How can I tell if a model fits my data?
quant-nist-residuals.note: Official statistical guidance supporting residual analysis and the inadequacy of R-squared alone for model validation. The source dataset and figures are not reproduced.

quant-nist-weighted.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 4.1.4.3: Weighted Least Squares Regression.
quant-nist-weighted.note: Official discussion of nonconstant error variance, relative precision weights, and uncertainty in estimated weights. No automatic concentration-based weighting rule is prescribed.

quant-ich-q2.title: ICH (2023; error corrections 2025). Q2(R2): Validation of Analytical Procedures.
quant-ich-q2.note: Official final guideline with 2025 error corrections, sections 3.2.3.3–3.2.3.5: linear-response DL/QL estimates and subsequent performance validation. Its pharmaceutical analytical-procedure scope is not treated as a universal omics rule. EMA current-version listing was checked on 2026-10-06; the ICH-hosted final PDF was read. ICH copyright acknowledged; original teaching explanations are not ICH-endorsed translations.

quant-vim-detection.title: JCGM. International Vocabulary of Metrology, VIM3, entry 4.18: detection limit.
quant-vim-detection.note: Official definition links detection capability to the measurement procedure and both false-presence and false-absence probabilities. No numerical error probabilities are inferred from the teaching example.

quant-experimental-units.title: Lazic, Clarke-Williams & Munafò (2018). What exactly is N in cell culture and animal experiments? PLOS Biology 16, e2005282.
quant-experimental-units.note: Original methodological study defining biological, experimental, and observational units and conditions for genuine replication. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pbio.2005282. Unit hierarchy is applied to independently constructed MS examples; study prevalence figures are not generalized.

quant-nist-blocking.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 5.3.3.2: Randomized block designs.
quant-nist-blocking.note: Official statistical guidance supporting blocking of nuisance factors and randomization within blocks. The 12-unit allocation and rank calculation are independently constructed, not sample-size advice.

quant-nist-nested.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 5.5.5: How can I account for nested variation (restricted randomization)?
quant-nist-nested.note: Official guidance distinguishing hierarchical variation and experimental-unit levels. Does not prescribe one statistical model for all biological studies.

quant-nist-sample-size.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 7.2.2.2: Sample sizes required.
quant-nist-sample-size.note: Official examples show dependence of sample-size planning on variability, detectable difference, and decision-error probabilities. No universal replicate count or source formula is imposed on MS experiments.

quant-batch-correction.title: Wehrens et al. (2016). Improved batch correction in untargeted MS-based metabolomics. Metabolomics 12, 88.
quant-batch-correction.note: Primary comparison across three untargeted plant-metabolomics datasets. DOI: 10.1007/s11306-016-1015-8. Supports data-, design-, and QC-dependent correction performance; no method ranking or universal QC frequency is transferred. Publisher full text and PubMed metadata checked.

prot-fasp.title: Wiśniewski et al. (2009). Universal sample preparation method for proteome analysis. Nature Methods 6, 359–362.
prot-fasp.note: Primary FASP demonstration. Supports detergent exchange and on-filter digestion as one preparation strategy, not universal superiority.

prot-sp3.title: Hughes et al. (2014). Ultrasensitive proteome analysis using paramagnetic bead technology. Molecular Systems Biology 10, 757.
prot-sp3.note: Primary SP3 demonstration. Supports bead-based preparation and low-input examples within the tested scope.

prot-trypsin.title: Olsen, Ong & Mann (2004). Trypsin cleaves exclusively C-terminal to arginine and lysine residues. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 3, 608–614.
prot-trypsin.note: Primary enzyme-specificity study. The Guide uses a separately declared K/R-except-before-P teaching rule and makes no complete-digestion guarantee.

prot-miape-ms.title: Taylor et al. (2008). Guidelines for reporting the use of mass spectrometry in proteomics. Nature Biotechnology 26, 860–861.
prot-miape-ms.note: HUPO-PSI reporting guidance. Reporting requirements do not certify analytical validity.

prot-mzidentml.title: Vizcaíno et al. (2017). The mzIdentML Data Standard Version 1.2, Supporting Advances in Proteome Informatics. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 16, 1275–1285.
prot-mzidentml.note: Standards paper supporting spectrum, peptide, database-sequence and protein-group evidence links. Version 1.2 is cited for these concepts, not asserted to be the newest release.

prot-proteotypic.title: Mallick et al. (2007). Computational prediction of proteotypic peptides for quantitative proteomics. Nature Biotechnology 25, 125–131.
prot-proteotypic.note: Primary study of preferential peptide observability across platforms. Does not make observability equivalent to sequence uniqueness or a validated assay.

prot-aqua.title: Gerber et al. (2003). Absolute quantification of proteins and phosphoproteins from cell lysates by tandem MS. PNAS 100, 6940–6945.
prot-aqua.note: Primary AQUA demonstration using stable-isotope peptide standards. The recovery-bias example is original teaching arithmetic, not data from this study.

prot-miape-msi.title: Binz et al. (2008). Guidelines for reporting the use of mass spectrometry informatics in proteomics. Nature Biotechnology 26, 862.
prot-miape-msi.note: HUPO-PSI guidance for documenting identification and validation methods.

prot-sequest.title: Eng et al. (2008). A Fast SEQUEST Cross Correlation Algorithm. Journal of Proteome Research 7, 4598–4602.
prot-sequest.note: Primary scoring-method paper. Supports method-specific candidate scoring; scores are not treated as universal probabilities.

prot-peptideprophet.title: Keller et al. (2002). Empirical statistical model to estimate the accuracy of peptide identifications made by MS/MS and database search. Analytical Chemistry 74, 5383–5392.
prot-peptideprophet.note: Primary PeptideProphet paper supporting statistical assignment-confidence modeling and its dependence on model and data.

prot-proteinprophet.title: Nesvizhskii et al. (2003). A Statistical Model for Identifying Proteins by Tandem Mass Spectrometry. Analytical Chemistry 75, 4646–4658.
prot-proteinprophet.note: Primary ProteinProphet paper supporting probabilistic protein inference and handling of shared peptide evidence. Constructed A/B/p/q/r examples are original.

prot-protein-reporting.title: Seymour et al. (2014). A standardized framing for reporting protein identifications in mzIdentML 1.2. Proteomics 14, 2389–2399.
prot-protein-reporting.note: Standards guidance distinguishing protein groups, leading proteins and group representatives. Does not equate a representative accession with unique experimental evidence.

prot-proforma.title: LeDuc et al. (2022). Proteomics Standards Initiative’s ProForma 2.0: Unifying the Encoding of Proteoforms and Peptidoforms. Journal of Proteome Research 21, 1189–1195.
prot-proforma.note: Standards paper covering modified sequences, natural/chemical/artifactual changes and positional ambiguity. No claim that notation validates a chemical identity or that version 2.0 is the latest specification.

prot-unimod-phospho.title: Unimod. Phospho, accession 21.
prot-unimod-phospho.note: Official curated modification record; monoisotopic increment 79.966331 Da, composition H O(3) P. Viewed 2026-10-06. The m/z calculations assume unchanged charge and otherwise identical ion composition.

prot-enrichment.title: Arribas Diez et al. (2021). Zirconium(IV)-IMAC Revisited: Improved Performance and Phosphoproteome Coverage by Magnetic Microparticles for Phosphopeptide Affinity Enrichment. Journal of Proteome Research 20, 453–462.
prot-enrichment.note: Primary comparison supports condition-dependent overlap and selectivity among phosphopeptide enrichment chemistries; no universal-best-method claim.

prot-ascore.title: Beausoleil et al. (2006). A probability-based approach for high-throughput protein phosphorylation analysis and site localization. Nature Biotechnology 24, 1285–1292.
prot-ascore.note: Primary Ascore paper supports site-determining fragment evidence. ASSTK is an original, explicitly simplified teaching example, not a spectrum from this paper.

prot-ptmprophet.title: Shteynberg et al. (2019). PTMProphet: Fast and Accurate Mass Modification Localization for the Trans-Proteomic Pipeline. Journal of Proteome Research 18, 4262–4272.
prot-ptmprophet.note: Primary localization-model paper supporting site probabilities and false localization rate estimation. No numerical cutoff is prescribed universally.

prot-stoichiometry.title: Wu et al. (2011). A large-scale method to measure absolute protein phosphorylation stoichiometries. Nature Methods 8, 677–683.
prot-stoichiometry.note: Primary occupancy-method paper supporting the distinction between modified amount, relative occupancy change and absolute stoichiometry; simple 100/200-unit arithmetic is original.

prot-unimod-oxidation.title: Unimod. Oxidation, accession 35.
prot-unimod-oxidation.note: Official modification database record with multiple residue-specific classifications including post-translational, artifact and chemical derivative. Viewed 2026-10-06. Record-level Verified field is No; used to illustrate representational breadth, not certify biological origin.

prot-proteotypic-context.title: Wilhelm et al. (2014). Mass-spectrometry-based draft of the human proteome. Nature 509, 582–587.
prot-proteotypic-context.note: Primary study, Extended Data Figure 10b, supports chemical-label dependence of peptide observability. Used for this methodological point only, not for a protein or disease catalog.

small-formula-rules.title: Kind and Fiehn (2007). Seven Golden Rules for heuristic filtering of molecular formulas obtained by accurate mass spectrometry. BMC Bioinformatics 8, 105.
small-formula-rules.note: Primary method paper. Supports formula filtering with isotope, element, and chemical constraints; no benchmark success rate or universal exclusion rule is adopted.

small-formula-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Molecular formula, entry M03987.
small-formula-definition.note: Official definition of molecular formula. Indexed official definition verified; direct HTML retrieval returned 403. The composition-versus-structure teaching distinction is explained in original prose.

small-isomer-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Isomer, entry I03289.
small-isomer-definition.note: Official definition: same atomic composition with different constitutional or stereochemical formulas. Official indexed PDF verified; direct HTML retrieval returned 403.

small-massbank.title: MassBank consortium. About MassBank.
small-massbank.note: Official description of a reference spectral library and chemical/experimental record metadata. No coverage or accuracy benchmark is inferred.

small-lipid-notation.title: Liebisch et al. (2020). Update on LIPID MAPS classification, nomenclature, and shorthand notation for MS-derived lipid structures. Journal of Lipid Research 61, 1539–1555.
small-lipid-notation.note: Community nomenclature standard. Supports evidence-dependent naming, chain composition, sn positions, double-bond information, and DBE qualifications. The simplified examples are restricted to unmodified diacyl PC.

small-lipid-official.title: LIPID MAPS. Lipid nomenclature and shorthand resources.
small-lipid-official.note: Official current landing page for full nomenclature and fast-track rules. The old shorthand_nomenclature URL returned 404 and is not used.

small-lipid-checklist-form.title: Lipidomics Standards Initiative. Lipid class description.
small-lipid-checklist-form.note: Official reporting form: polarity, ion forms, fragments, standards, isotope overlap, background, isomer overlap, and quantification fields. Read-only inspection; no form submitted.

small-lipid-class-fragments.title: Lipidomics Standards Initiative. Lipid class specific fragments.
small-lipid-class-fragments.note: Official table lists the phosphocholine product near m/z 184.0733 for protonated PC and SM and limits the structural claim to sum composition.

small-lipid-monitoring.title: Lipidomics Standards Initiative. MS – Lipid ion monitoring.
small-lipid-monitoring.note: Official guidance relating measurement methods to structural detail. Example method labels are not treated as universal sufficiency guarantees.

small-ozid.title: Thomas et al. (2008). Ozone-induced dissociation: elucidation of double bond position within mass-selected lipid ions. Analytical Chemistry 80, 303–311.
small-ozid.note: Primary methodological report. Used only for the role of ozone-induced dissociation in double-bond localization, not for generalized isomer resolution or quantification claims.

small-pb.title: Hu, Xia, and Ma (2021). Comprehensive Structural Characterization of Lipids by Coupling Paternò–Büchi Reaction and Tandem Mass Spectrometry. Methods in Molecular Biology 2306, 53–60.
small-pb.note: Original methods chapter by method developers. Abstract verifies double-bond-sensitive photochemical derivatization and diagnostic MS/MS; no protocol conditions or performance claims are reproduced.

small-lipid-separation.title: Lipidomics Standards Initiative. Separation MS.
small-lipid-separation.note: Official guidance on retention context and demonstrating lipid-isomer discrimination with standards or appropriate retention models.

small-lipid-reporting.title: Kopczynski et al. (2024). The lipidomics reporting checklist a framework for transparency of lipidomic experiments and repurposing resource data. Journal of Lipid Research 65, 100621.
small-lipid-reporting.note: Primary community reporting framework. Supports documenting identification, quantification, and quality information; no checklist completion implies automatic analytical validity.

small-im-reporting.title: Gabelica et al. (2019). Recommendations for reporting ion mobility Mass Spectrometry measurements. Mass Spectrometry Reviews 38, 291–320.
small-im-reporting.note: Community reporting recommendations. Supports separating arrival time, mobility, and model-derived CCS; reporting ion species, gas, temperature, reduced field, calibration, and uncertainty.

small-im-definition.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Ion mobility spectrometry, entry 12442.
small-im-definition.note: Official definition based on IUPAC Recommendations 2013: gas-phase separation under an electric field.

small-im-interlab.title: Stow et al. (2017). An Interlaboratory Evaluation of Drift Tube Ion Mobility-Mass Spectrometry Collision Cross Section Measurements. Analytical Chemistry 89, 9048–9055.
small-im-interlab.note: Primary interlaboratory comparison of stepped-field and calibrated single-field nitrogen CCS. Numerical performance is not generalized to other platforms or methods.

small-im-twave.title: Shvartsburg and Smith (2008). Fundamentals of Traveling Wave Ion Mobility Spectrometry. Analytical Chemistry 80, 9689–9699.
small-im-twave.note: Primary theoretical and numerical study. Supports nonlinear traveling-wave transport versus uniform-field drift motion and method-specific conversion requirements.

small-im-tims.title: Fernandez-Lima et al. (2011). Gas-phase separation using a trapped ion mobility spectrometer. International Journal for Ion Mobility Spectrometry 14, 93–98.
small-im-tims.note: Primary TIMS principles paper. Supports opposing gas flow and electric field with controlled release; no commercial resolving-power claim is adopted.

small-im-dms.title: Krylov et al. (2010). Selection and generation of waveforms for differential mobility spectrometry. Review of Scientific Instruments 81, 024101.
small-im-dms.note: Primary theory/experiment paper. Supports separation based on field-dependent mobility and waveform-dependent compensation behavior.

small-im-database.title: Zheng et al. (2017). A structural examination and collision cross section database for over 500 metabolites and xenobiotics using drift tube ion mobility spectrometry. Chemical Science 8, 7724–7736.
small-im-database.note: Primary nitrogen drift-tube CCS study of small molecules and different ion forms. Supports CCS as an additional candidate constraint, not a universal unique identifier.

struct-xl-community.title: Leitner et al. (2020). Toward Increased Reliability, Transparency, and Accessibility in Cross-linking Mass Spectrometry. Structure 28, 1259–1268.
struct-xl-community.note: Community reporting recommendations. Supports explicit chemistry, reporting levels, data accessibility, and separate treatment of self and heteromeric link categories. Not a universal distance-cutoff or performance standard.

struct-xl-dsso.title: Kao et al. (2011). Development of a Novel Cross-linking Strategy for Fast and Accurate Identification of Cross-linked Peptides of Protein Complexes. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 10, M110.002212.
struct-xl-dsso.note: Primary DSSO method. Supports distinguishable interlink, intralink/loop, and dead-end products and MS-cleavable-linker-assisted partner identification. Does not establish a guarantee for every candidate spectrum.

struct-xl-target-decoy.title: Walzthoeni et al. (2012). False discovery rate estimation for cross-linked peptides identified by mass spectrometry. Nature Methods 9, 901–903.
struct-xl-target-decoy.note: Primary target-decoy strategy for crosslinked-peptide assignments. The candidate-pair arithmetic is original, and no universal target-decoy counting formula is supplied.

struct-xl-error-levels.title: Fischer and Rappsilber (2017). Quirks of Error Estimation in Cross-Linking/Mass Spectrometry. Analytical Chemistry 89, 3829–3833.
struct-xl-error-levels.note: Primary analysis of error at different aggregation levels, particularly residue and protein pairs. The 90/10 CSM illustration is invented known-label arithmetic, not paper data or an FDR estimator.

struct-xl-distance.title: Bullock et al. (2016). The Importance of Non-accessible Crosslinks and Solvent Accessible Surface Distance in Modeling Proteins with Restraints From Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 15, 2491–2500.
struct-xl-distance.note: Primary modeling study comparing distance representations and accessibility. Used for restraint interpretation, without reproducing benchmark outcomes or adopting a fixed distance cutoff.

struct-xl-benchmark.title: Beveridge et al. (2020). A synthetic peptide library for benchmarking crosslinking-mass spectrometry search engines for proteins and protein complexes. Nature Communications 11, 742.
struct-xl-benchmark.note: Primary experimental reference-library study. Cited only to distinguish genuine benchmark materials from this packet’s original logic examples; no search-engine ranking or performance rate is reproduced.

struct-glyco-mirage.title: Lisacek et al. (2026; published online 2025). Update and New Implementation of the MIRAGE Reporting Guidelines for Mass Spectrometry Experiments in Glycoscience. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 25, 101473.
struct-glyco-mirage.note: Updated community reporting guidance with explicit glycoproteomics scope, composition/structure uncertainty, microheterogeneity and site occupancy. Online publication 2025-11-24; collection date February 2026. Not a claim that reporting compliance proves identification.

struct-glyco-glycoform.title: IUPAC Gold Book. Glycoform, entry 09815.
struct-glyco-glycoform.note: Official definition, based on IUPAC Recommendations 2018. Supports whole-glycoprotein glycosylation-pattern meaning and heterogeneity from structures or site occupancy. Viewed 2026-10-06.

struct-glyco-fragmentation.title: Riley et al. (2020). Optimal Dissociation Methods Differ for N- and O-Glycopeptides. Journal of Proteome Research 19, 3286–3301.
struct-glyco-fragmentation.note: Primary comparison of collision-, electron-, and hybrid-fragmentation evidence. Supports the distinct requirements of peptide identity and glycosite evidence. No universal optimal energy, platform ranking, or identification yield is adopted.

struct-glyco-opair.title: Lu et al. (2020). O-Pair Search with MetaMorpheus for O-glycopeptide characterization. Nature Methods 17, 1133–1138.
struct-glyco-opair.note: Primary method separating peptide identification and O-glycosite localization with paired spectra and probability-based inference. ASTK is an original fragment-membership example, not study data.

struct-glyco-snfg.title: Symbol Nomenclature for Glycans (SNFG). Official notation guidance hosted by NCBI.
struct-glyco-snfg.note: Official standard resource, including conventions for ambiguous monosaccharides, linkages and mixtures. Used to preserve uncertainty in representations; a valid drawing is not analytical proof.

struct-glyco-search.title: Polasky et al. (2020). Fast and comprehensive N- and O-glycoproteomics analysis with MSFragger-Glyco. Nature Methods 17, 1125–1132.
struct-glyco-search.note: Primary search method supports documenting glycan candidate sets and effects of expanding searches. No speed or identification gain is reproduced or generalized.

struct-glyco-fdr.title: Liu et al. (2017). pGlyco 2.0 enables precision N-glycoproteomics with comprehensive quality control and one-step mass spectrometry for intact glycopeptide identification. Nature Communications 8, 438.
struct-glyco-fdr.note: Primary method explicitly treating peptide-component, glycan-component and joint errors in glycopeptide-spectrum matches (GPSMs). Distinct-entity aggregation, site localization and glycan linkage claims require separate consideration; this is not a universal guarantee for newer workflows.

struct-phospho-enrichment.title: Yue, Schunter, and Hummon (2015). Comparing Multistep Immobilized Metal Affinity Chromatography and Multistep TiO2 Methods for Phosphopeptide Enrichment. Analytical Chemistry 87, 8837–8844.
struct-phospho-enrichment.note: Primary enrichment comparison supports condition-dependent and complementary coverage. Selectivity-versus-recovery arithmetic is original, not a result of the paper; no universal best method is declared.

struct-phospho-reproducibility.title: Tape et al. (2014). Reproducible Automated Phosphopeptide Enrichment Using Magnetic TiO2 and Ti-IMAC. Analytical Chemistry 86, 10296–10302.
struct-phospho-reproducibility.note: Primary work measuring recovery and preparation reproducibility. Used to motivate assessing both, not to transfer reported performance to a different preparation.

struct-phospho-flr.title: Ramsbottom et al. (2022). Method for Independent Estimation of the False Localization Rate for Phosphoproteomics. Journal of Proteome Research 21, 1603–1615.
struct-phospho-flr.note: Primary decoy-residue localization-error methodology. Supports independent FLR assessment and care over aggregation. No threshold is presented as universally calibrated.

struct-phospho-dia.title: Bekker-Jensen et al. (2020). Rapid and site-specific deep phosphoproteome profiling by data-independent acquisition without the need for spectral libraries. Nature Communications 11, 787.
struct-phospho-dia.note: Primary DIA method incorporating fragment and chromatographic information into phosphorylation localization. Not evidence that every DIA assignment or transferred library entry is localized.

struct-phospho-protein-adjustment.title: Wu et al. (2011). Correct Interpretation of Comprehensive Phosphorylation Dynamics Requires Normalization by Protein Expression Changes. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics 10, M111.009654.
struct-phospho-protein-adjustment.note: Primary study showing the contribution of parent-protein abundance to phosphopeptide change. The 3/2 ratio and occupancy alternatives are original examples under constant response and recovery.

spatial-msi-reporting.title: McDonnell et al. (2015; published online 2014). Discussion point: reporting guidelines for mass spectrometry imaging. Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry 407, 2035–2045.
spatial-msi-reporting.note: Community reporting proposal. Supports reporting preparation, acquisition, extraction, normalization, scales and image processing. Institutional full-text PDF inspected. Not a certification that an image represents concentration or a clinical conclusion.

spatial-resolution-pattern.title: Fagerer et al. (2015). Resolution pattern for mass spectrometry imaging. Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry 29, 1019–1024.
spatial-resolution-pattern.note: Primary resolution-test-pattern study; publisher abstract and metadata verified. Supports testing actual feature separation. The packet does not impose a universal terminology convention, edge criterion, or resolution limit.

spatial-oversampling.title: Duncan and Lanekoff (2018). Oversampling To Improve Spatial Resolution for Liquid Extraction Mass Spectrometry Imaging. Analytical Chemistry 90, 2451–2455.
spatial-oversampling.note: Primary nano-DESI study demonstrating conditional benefit of oversampling. Publisher abstract inspected. No universal improvement, depletion mechanism, pixel pitch, or instrument capability is inferred.

spatial-msi-annotation.title: Palmer et al. (2017; published online 2016). FDR-controlled metabolite annotation for high-resolution imaging mass spectrometry. Nature Methods 14, 57–60.
spatial-msi-annotation.note: Primary framework for molecular-sum-formula-level annotation. PubMed abstract and publisher metadata checked; direct publisher open encountered an access redirect. No unique-isomer or concentration claim is inferred from formula-level FDR.

spatial-msi-normalization.title: Deininger et al. (2011). Normalization in MALDI-TOF imaging datasets of proteins: practical considerations. Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry 401, 167–181.
spatial-msi-normalization.note: Primary analysis of normalization artifacts. Publisher full text and indexed PMC text inspected; direct PMC access encountered a bot check. Supports denominator-dependent distortion, not a universal ranking of normalization procedures. The 10/100 and 10/200 example is original.

spatial-autocorrelation.title: Cassese et al. (2016). Spatial Autocorrelation in Mass Spectrometry Imaging. Analytical Chemistry 88, 5871–5878.
spatial-autocorrelation.note: Primary within-sample statistical study; publisher abstract and metadata checked. Supports spatial dependence of neighboring MSI observations. No numerical discovery-rate improvement or mandatory model is transferred to this guide.

spatial-imzml.title: Schramm et al. (2012). imzML—a common data format for the flexible exchange and processing of mass spectrometry imaging data. Journal of Proteomics 75, 5106–5110.
spatial-imzml.note: Original community format description; PubMed indexed abstract/metadata and official imzML repository inspected. Supports exchange of metadata and spectral data, not validation of chemical identity or biological conclusions.

spatial-scp-recommendations.title: Gatto et al. (2023). Initial recommendations for performing, benchmarking and reporting single-cell proteomics experiments. Nature Methods 20, 375–386.
spatial-scp-recommendations.note: Original community recommendations/Perspective. Supports randomization, quantitative quality, negative controls, missingness and filtering sensitivity. Public primary text inspected during research; publisher open may redirect. Not an experimental performance benchmark or mandatory universal threshold.

spatial-scope2.title: Specht et al. (2021). Single-cell proteomic and transcriptomic analysis of macrophage heterogeneity using SCoPE2. Genome Biology 22, 50.
spatial-scope2.note: Primary method; publisher full text inspected. Supports isobaric channel workflow, carrier versus reference roles, reporter-ion quantification and coisolation. Diluted bulk standards are distinguished from real single cells; no dataset-wide coverage is attributed to every cell.

spatial-carrier-limit.title: Cheung et al. (2021; published online 2020). Defining the carrier proteome limit for single-cell proteomics. Nature Methods 18, 76–83.
spatial-carrier-limit.note: Primary controlled carrier and ion-sampling study, verified through public primary records. Supports setup-dependent quantitative tradeoffs; no universal carrier ratio is recommended. The Poisson calculation is an independent idealized model, not experimental counts from the paper.

spatial-scp-accuracy.title: Ctortecka et al. (2022). Quantitative Accuracy and Precision in Multiplexed Single-Cell Proteomics. Analytical Chemistry 94, 2434–2443.
spatial-scp-accuracy.note: Primary analytical study using low-input bulk HeLa digest aliquots, not individually isolated cells. PubMed metadata and public primary full text verified. Supports separating identification counts from quantitative usability; no numerical carrier limit or method ranking is generalized.

spatial-clsi-ep17.title: CLSI (2012). EP17-A2: Evaluation of Detection Capability for Clinical Laboratory Measurement Procedures; Approved Guideline—Second Edition.
spatial-clsi-ep17.note: Official standard overview and public scope verified; second edition published 2012 and reaffirmed 2017. Full paid standard not claimed to have been inspected. Supports distinguishing blank, detection and quantification capability; not a universal discovery-proteomics acceptance rule.

spatial-pseudoreplication.title: Zimmerman, Espeland and Langefeld (2021). A practical solution to pseudoreplication bias in single-cell studies. Nature Communications 12, 738.
spatial-pseudoreplication.note: Primary analysis in single-cell RNA sequencing. Only the hierarchical experimental-unit principle is transferred to proteomics. No RNA-specific model, power result or threshold is transferred. Donor/cell counts are original teaching examples.

spatial-clsi-terminology.title: CLSI Harmonized Terminology Database. Limit of blank entry.
spatial-clsi-terminology.note: Official term-specific public entry inspected directly on 2026-10-06. Supports a probability-defined upper boundary for blank results and distinction from detection capability. The known-normal percentile arithmetic is original and explicitly excludes finite-sample estimation uncertainty.

spatial-msi-preparation.title: Yang and Caprioli (2011). Matrix Sublimation/Recrystallization for Imaging Proteins by Mass Spectrometry at High Spatial Resolution. Analytical Chemistry 83, 5728–5734.
spatial-msi-preparation.note: Primary preparation study; publisher abstract and indexed public full text inspected. Examines washing, section thickness, matrix amount and recrystallization. No numerical protocol, universal preparation optimum or resolution specification is transferred.

comp-prosit.title: Gessulat et al. (2019). Prosit: proteome-wide prediction of peptide tandem mass spectra by deep learning. Nature Methods 16, 509–518.
comp-prosit.note: Primary peptide-intensity and retention prediction study. Used as a defined model example, not a universal performance guarantee or identification-confidence calibration.

comp-massformer.title: Young, Röst & Wang (2024). Tandem mass spectrum prediction for small molecules using graph transformers. Nature Machine Intelligence 6, 404–416.
comp-massformer.note: Primary small-molecule spectrum-prediction study. Supports the distinction between molecular-graph prediction and peptide-specific models; no reported superiority is extrapolated.

comp-multispecies.title: Wen & Noble (2024). A multi-species benchmark for training and validating mass spectrometry proteomics machine learning models. Scientific Data 11, 1207.
comp-multispecies.note: Primary benchmark with explicit removal of shared peptide sequences across species. Search-derived labels are not presented here as independently known molecular truth.

comp-massspecgym.title: Bushuiev et al. (2024). MassSpecGym: A benchmark for the discovery and identification of molecules. NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks Track.
comp-massspecgym.note: Primary benchmark defining molecular retrieval, generation, spectrum simulation, and a generalization-demanding split. Dataset scope is not a guarantee for all structures or acquisition settings.

comp-similarity.title: Li et al. (2021). Spectral entropy outperforms MS/MS dot product similarity for small-molecule compound identification. Nature Methods 18, 1524–1531.
comp-similarity.note: Primary spectral-similarity comparison. The educational text does not transfer reported cutoffs, error rates, or metric superiority beyond the studied comparisons. Vector examples are original constructed arithmetic.

comp-deeplc.title: Bouwmeester et al. (2021). DeepLC can predict retention times for peptides that carry as-yet unseen modifications. Nature Methods 18, 1363–1369.
comp-deeplc.note: Primary retention-prediction study using composition-based modification representation. Does not support unrestricted transfer to every modification or chromatographic setup.

comp-irt.title: Escher et al. (2012). Using iRT, a normalized retention time for more targeted measurement of peptides. Proteomics 12, 1111–1121.
comp-irt.note: Primary reference-scale approach for peptide retention. DOI: 10.1002/pmic.201100463. Dimensionless reference values require mapping to local chromatographic time.

comp-calibration.title: Guo, Pleiss, Sun & Weinberger (2017). On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks. Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 70, 1321–1330.
comp-calibration.note: Primary general machine-learning calibration methodology; experiments concern image and document classification, not validation of an MS workflow. The confidence-bin example is original and synthetic.

comp-benchmark-guidelines.title: Weber et al. (2019). Essential guidelines for computational method benchmarking. Genome Biology 20, 125.
comp-benchmark-guidelines.note: Authors’ original methodological guidelines for designing benchmarks. Used for scope, fairness, and reproducibility principles, not as an experimental comparison of MS tools.

comp-synthetic.title: Zolg et al. (2017). Building ProteomeTools based on a complete synthetic human proteome. Nature Methods 14, 259–262.
comp-synthetic.note: Primary synthetic-peptide resource. Intended synthesis identities alone do not establish purity or the identity of every acquired spectrum.

comp-tdc-bias.title: Danilova et al. (2019). Bias in False Discovery Rate Estimation in Mass-Spectrometry-Based Peptide Identification. Journal of Proteome Research 18, 2354–2358.
comp-tdc-bias.note: Primary methodological analysis of false-target/decoy behavior, biased scoring and correlated spectra. DOI: 10.1021/acs.jproteome.8b00991. Metadata and abstract verified; no uninspected numerical results are claimed.

comp-entrapment.title: Wen et al. (2025). Assessment of false discovery rate control in tandem mass spectrometry analysis using entrapment. Nature Methods 22, 1454–1463.
comp-entrapment.note: Primary methodological study defining entrapment estimators and their assumptions, and stating a conservative target-decoy thresholding procedure. The packet’s counts are synthetic and do not validate its assumptions.

comp-mztab.title: HUPO-PSI. mzTab: Reporting MS-based Proteomics and Metabolomics Results.
comp-mztab.note: Official format overview with the mzTab 1.0 and mzTab-M 2.0 resources. Supports lightweight result exchange and links to detailed evidence; no claim that every mzTab variant is interchangeable.

comp-mscv.title: Mayer et al. (2013). The HUPO proteomics standards initiative—mass spectrometry controlled vocabulary. Database 2013, bat009.
comp-mscv.note: Original PSI-MS controlled-vocabulary publication. DOI: 10.1093/database/bat009. Supports semantic annotation and stable concept identifiers; conformance does not establish scientific truth.

comp-sdrf.title: Dai et al. (2021). A proteomics sample metadata representation for multiomics integration and big data analysis. Nature Communications 12, 5854.
comp-sdrf.note: Primary MAGE-TAB/SDRF-Proteomics standard describing sample-to-file relationships, multiplexing, fractions, and experimental factors. The packet’s 3-sample/2-fraction example is constructed.

comp-prov.title: W3C (2013). PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model. W3C Recommendation, 30 April 2013.
comp-prov.note: Official domain-independent provenance model of entities, activities, derivation, and responsibility. It is not an MS file format or a requirement to use a particular workflow engine.

comp-px-guidelines.title: ProteomeXchange Consortium (2019). Data Submission Guidelines, version 3.0.1, 13 October 2019.
comp-px-guidelines.note: Official published guidance distinguishing raw data, result files, and metadata and explaining linked submissions. Cited for durable concepts, not asserted to supersede current repository-specific requirements.
